Register a geometry emitter

Source: R/emitters.R
register_geom_3d.Rd

Register a geometry emitter

Usage

register_geom_3d(
  geom,
  emit,
  aesthetics = character(),
  setup_data = NULL,
  stat_adapter = NULL,
  position_check = NULL,
  replace = FALSE,
  prepare_data = NULL,
  prepare_aesthetics = NULL,
  parameters = list(),
  default_z = 0,
  positions = "nudge",
  extents = list(),
  tween = c("group", "row", "path", "polygon"),
  space = NULL
)

Arguments

geom

A ggplot2 geom prototype.

emit

Function accepting data, params and panel_params.

aesthetics

Additional supported aesthetics.

setup_data

Optional geometry setup function.

stat_adapter

Optional stat prototype.

position_check

Optional extra position validation, a function of the position and the panel's scales that signals an error.

replace

Whether to replace an existing registration.

prepare_data, prepare_aesthetics

Optional preparation functions applied to every layer drawing the geom inside coord_3d(): prepare_data(data) receives the layer data, prepare_aesthetics(out, data, plot, params) the evaluated aesthetics with the layer data, plot and layer parameters.

parameters

Named list of further drawing parameters the geom accepts, with their defaults. They reach the emitter in params.

default_z

Height of a layer without a z mapping. The default 0 trains the z scale; -Inf places the layer on the floor without training it.

positions

Position adjustments the geometry accepts besides identity: any of "nudge" (position_nudge_3d()), "jitter" (position_jitter_3d()), "dodge" (position_dodge_3d()), "stack" (position_stack_3d(), position_fill_3d()) and "planar" (ggplot2's own nudge, jitter and dodge, which move x and y only).

extents

Named list, by axis "x", "y", "z", of the columns holding the geometry's interval along that axis, as character vectors c(lower = , upper = , centre = ); lower or centre may be NA. Stacking and dodging read and rewrite these columns. An axis not listed takes its own coordinate as both the interval end and the anchor.

tween

How tween_3d() pairs the layer's rows between two states. "row": each row is one mark (points, text, columns), paired by group and order. "path" and "polygon": the rows of a group form an open or closed line, resampled by arc length when the two states differ in length. "group" (default): the rows of a group form one shape (a surface, a mesh) that morphs row by row when its row count is unchanged and cross-fades otherwise.

space

Optional function of data, params and panel_params returning a space specification. Layer-owned canonical geometry then shares coordinate munching and remunches against the final camera and viewport.

Value

NULL invisibly. Registers the emitter for subsequent layers.

Details

The emitter receives scale-transformed positions normalised to the panel box. It returns a scene packet from new_scene_packet(). Vertices hold x, y, z; corners index vertices; primitive offsets index corners. Style IDs index the style table. Source rows and layer IDs preserve input identity.

Examples

GeomTriangle3D <- ggplot2::ggproto("GeomTriangle3D", ggplot2::Geom,
  required_aes = c("x", "y", "z"),
  default_aes = ggplot2::aes(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 1),
  draw_key = ggplot2::draw_key_polygon)
emit_triangle <- function(data, params, panel_params) {
  stopifnot(nrow(data) == 3L)
  new_scene_packet(
    vertices = list(x = as.double(data$x), y = as.double(data$y),
                    z = as.double(data$z)),
    corners = list(vertex = 1:3, source_row = as.integer(data$.source)),
    faces = list(offset = 1L, count = 3L, style_id = 1L,
      source_row = as.integer(data$.source[1]),
      layer_id = as.integer(data$.layer[1]), opacity = data$alpha[1]),
    styles = data.frame(style_id = 1L, fill = data$fill[1],
                        colour = NA_character_, shade = FALSE),
    panel_id = panel_params$panel_id)
}
register_geom_3d(GeomTriangle3D, emit_triangle, replace = TRUE)
triangle <- ggplot2::layer(geom = GeomTriangle3D, stat = "identity",
  position = "identity", params = list())
d <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1), z = c(0, 1, 1))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  layer_3d(triangle) + coord_3d()
